$comment: Extension campaign — two experiments exercising the monee solver
extensions end-to-end on the Stepper-based environment (the
RestorationEnvironmentBehavior drives physics through a persistent
monee.Stepper; see mango_energy_environments.base.monee.
create_physics_stepper).
Experiment 1  extension_islanding — A/B via the two scenario rows
(kind=clean vs kind=microgrid) on the typical
simbench_lv grid with identical seeds + failure_type=island
(each cut isolates a GENERATION-bearing subtree from the
slack, so the microgrid arm's promoted grid-former can
self-anchor the island while the clean arm de-energises it
— concentrated cuts strand load-only pockets that collapse
identically in both arms and never exercise islanding).
kind=microgrid enables monee's
islanding MILP and promotes every generator to
GridForming so sub-islands can self-anchor.  The
environment auto-selects monee's native gurobipy
backend for islanding nets (the island indicator
constraints are bilinear and cannot pass Pyomo's LP
writer — the failure mode that made the 2026-05 version
of this campaign KNOWN-FAILING).  The oracle variant
solves on the same islanding config, so the optimality
gap is like-for-like.  Islanding evidence lands in
network_changes.csv (islanded/rejoined events), the
nodes_deenergised / islanded_events_cum timeseries, and
outcomes.oracle_islanding.
Experiment 2  extension_temporal — gas linepack + thermal LTC
(LumpedThermalCapacitance) on simbench_lv_small
(LV-S, 1-LV-rural1 at CP density 0.5, slack-fed heat +
flow-sized pipes + 0.4x CPs so the born heat field stays
inside [313,403] K instead of saturating at the ~620 K
t_pu ceiling, while carrying the CHP / P2H / PowerToGas
CPs the deficit has to bite) to keep the per-step solve
cheap.  LTC runs with the first-step steady-state anchor so
junctions settle onto the physical field before inertia
engages, rather than cold-starting at the t_pu reference.
failure_type=generator with generator_carriers=[heat,gas]
(stratified so the lone PowerToGas AND a heat producer are
both failed) puts the deficit on the storage carriers — a
mix of electrical-generator failures leaves gas/heat intact
and never draws linepack or thermal mass.  Both
scenario rows run the same multi-hour physical horizon at
physics_time_scale=1 (sim clock = physical time, so agent
message/poll delays and the physics dt share one unit).
physics_interval_s=10 => dt 10 s; simulation_duration_s=
21600 => 6 h, 2160 steps.  sector_timescale sets physical
control cadences (elec 30s, gas 120s, heat 600s poll).
Periodic-only physics solving (ablation cooldown/max_acts)
settles the physics at CONVERGED agent states each step
rather than re-solving mid-negotiation on every setpoint
write (which gave ~27% infeasible-then-stale solves at the
slow real-time cadence).  The
delta between the rows is the temporal extensions, so
the comparison isolates the storage-flexibility uplift
(linepack draw-down + thermal inertia riding through
the generator-failure deficit under tight slack).  The
oracle variant runs the receding run_temporal_oracle on
the identical step grid; per-step series land in
outcomes.oracle_temporal and the MAS trajectories in
timeseries.csv (linepack_total_kg, ltc_junction_t_*).
Both experiments use n_seeds=5 and the scare+oracle variants; scenario
rows share seeds per (grid, run), so every A/B delta is paired.
name: extension_campaign
$timeout_comment: task_timeout_s 5400 -> 9000 and slurm 02:00:00 -> 03:00:00. Two independent reasons. (1) 5400 was ALREADY too low for the scare microgrid arm on 20260728-143126: seed 1 timed out at 5716 s while seeds 0/2 ran 4282/4240 s. (2) extension_islanding's oracle_time_limit_s forwards to the pre-failure baseline LP, and _compute_baseline runs for EVERY task, not just the oracle — so a scare microgrid task's baseline cap goes 300 s -> 900 s, i.e. +600 s on top of durations that were already at the ceiling. Headroom is deliberate: slurm bills actual usage, so an over-generous cap costs nothing on tasks that finish early but prevents the seed-1 timeout recurring. slurm time must stay ABOVE task_timeout_s, else Slurm kills the task before its own timeout can write status.json.

experiments.$comment: Scenario row 1 = baseline (no islanding: sub-islands without a slack lose their load); row 2 = islanding extension + GridForming promotion. Same seeds and failure draws across rows. heat_mccormick on row 1 puts the clean arm on the SAME relaxed heat physics the microgrid arm needs for its MILP solve, so the paired delta isolates the islanding extension instead of confounding it with the heat relaxation.
experiments.name: extension_islanding
experiments.$oracle_budget_comment: oracle_time_limit_s=900 on BOTH rows. What this buys is SYMMETRY, not convergence. Before it, the arms were not convergence-matched: kind=microgrid silently picks up the 900 s _ORACLE_HARD_PRESET while kind=clean fell back to the 300 s default, so the paired A/B compared a 300 s oracle against a 900 s one — on 20260728-143126 that left the clean arm 3/5 time-limited at gaps up to 0.076 while certification read 50% overall. Setting the key also forwards it to the pre-failure baseline LP (runner._compute_baseline), which otherwise keeps its own 300 s _BASELINE_SOLVE_CAP_S, so it additionally closes the ratio asymmetry of dividing a 900 s post state by a 300 s baseline. DO NOT raise it further: 1800 was measured on seed 2 (microgrid, post-fix) and is REFUTED — gap 0.003799 -> 0.003780 and a BIT-IDENTICAL incumbent PWSF 0.982215 for 3x the task cost (1208 s -> 3608 s). The bound is asymptotic, so this arm will not certify at any budget; read it via the report's `usable` columns (feasible incumbent + valid dual bound) rather than `certified`. Also note the baseline moved pwsf_baseline 0.9880 -> 0.9856 at 1800 s — NOT a regression: the oracle maximises the near-lexicographic tier ladder (_ORACLE_TIER_WEIGHT 1e6/1e4/1e2/1), not PWSF's 8:4:2:1, so a better ladder solution can score marginally lower on PWSF. The budget is spent TWICE per oracle task (baseline + post-failure) and the baseline half lands on EVERY task including scare, so worst case is ~2*900 for oracle and observed-scare + ~600 s; see the top-level $timeout_comment for the timeouts that cover it.

experiments.$comment: Scenario row 1 = multi-hour horizon WITHOUT temporal extensions; row 2 = same horizon with gas linepack + thermal LTC. Heat+gas generator failures + tight slack (0.15) put the deficit on the storage carriers. physics_time_scale=1 (sim clock = physical time), interval 10 => dt 10s, dur 21600 => 6h/2160 steps; sector_timescale sets physical control cadences (elec 30s, gas 120s, heat 600s poll). Periodic-only physics solving (ablation cooldown/max_acts) settles at converged agent states each step; stays feasible (0% solve fail) with PWSF flat vs coarser intervals — benchmarked ~7 min MAS / ~3 min oracle per task at 6h on the tiny LV-S (each MILP ~0.09s). Note interval < elec poll (30s) so physics updates faster than agents observe; finer than 30s only refines trajectory resolution. Tuned LV-S keeps the per-step solve cheap.
experiments.name: extension_temporal
experiments.$ablation_comment: physics_time_scale=1 makes the sim clock physical time; pair it with periodic-only physics solving (huge cooldown + max_acts=0) so the physics settles at CONVERGED agent states each 10-s step instead of re-solving mid-negotiation on every setpoint write — the latter caused ~27% infeasible-then-stale solves at the slow real-time cadence. Applies to both scenario rows and both variants, so no A/B confound.
